lens: Continual learning / memory consolidation in biosignal representation learning. The audited normal-anchor drift (cosine 0.954 after Stage 1 -> 0.594 after Stage 4) is a measured, quantified forgetting curve inside a continual skeleton-JEPA body-representation learner; this direction treats that drift not as a residual weakness but as the central research object, and asks whether one cheap consolidation signal can repair it.
title: Don't Forget Normal: Quantifying and Repairing Anchor Drift in a Continual Skeleton-JEPA for Gait
one_sentence_question: Can one cheap consolidation signal — distilling the frozen Stage-0 normal centroid back into the encoder, an anchor-directional EWC penalty, or replay upweighting — cut the measured normal-anchor drift (cosine 0.954 -> 0.594) by at least half without degrading source-disjoint new-condition probe accuracy in a continual skeleton-JEPA?
why_novel: Reframes the project's single most robust, pre-registered negative result (normal-anchor cosine 0.954->0.594) as a quantified consolidation-failure curve, turning a weakness into the paper's object of study. (1) Introduces the 'normal anchor' as a label-free, cheap, continuously computable drift metric for body-representation continual learners — it needs no downstream labels, unlike standard forgetting/accuracy-based metrics. (2) Runs a controlled three-axes consolidation comparison (representation-space anchor distillation vs parameter-space anchor-directional EWC vs data-space replay) inside one identical SSL curriculum, which almost no skeleton/biosignal SSL work reports. (3) Proposes a mechanistic, causal twist: the label-aware group margin (which pushes condition centroids toward cosine 0.5) is hypothesized to actively manufacture the drift, so a key ablation localizes forgetting to the fine-tuning objective rather than to new-task data per se — a novel consolidation-vs-plasticity insight for JEPA-style clinical fine-tuning. (4) Gives the drift a clinical-safety framing: a gait model that forgets what 'normal' looks like is a deployment hazard, not a benchmark nuisance, which the BrainBodyFM audience is primed to care about.
workshop_fit: Direct hit on an explicitly listed topic — 'continual learning in biosignal contexts' — where biosignals include pose extracted from video. This edition emphasizes the motor side of the loop (movement, motor control, closed-loop interaction) and scaling/generalization techniques from robotics and embodied AI; a continual skeleton-JEPA over gait sits squarely in that intersection. The 5-page, non-archival, double-blind format fits a focused one-metric, three-intervention study whose centerpiece is a single drift-curve figure (before/after consolidation). No new data, no IRB changes, and ~1 hour of compute make it deliverable inside the Sep 5 AoE deadline.

decisive_experiments.name: Baseline re-verification (no retrain)
decisive_experiments.what: Reload the five frozen checkpoints, recompute the normal-anchor cosine at each stage end from the pooled 384-d target-encoder embeddings, and re-run the source_disjoint_probe (GroupKFold ridge) readouts on the Stage-4 encoder. Locks in the reference curve 0.954/0.839/0.707/0.594 and the video-disjoint 5-class baseline (0.564 acc / 0.495 macro-F1 from the fresh 2026-08-17 rerun).
decisive_experiments.cost: seconds (frozen checkpoints and pose caches already exist)
decisive_experiments.pre_registered_success: Reproduce Stage-4 normal-anchor cosine 0.594 within tolerance and freeze the metric recipe as the report template for all intervention runs.
decisive_experiments.key_metric: normal-anchor cosine per stage; video-disjoint 5-class probe

decisive_experiments.name: Anchor distillation (representation-space consolidation)
decisive_experiments.what: Freeze the Stage-0 target encoder and its pooled normal centroid c0 (unit-norm 384-d). During Stages 1-4 add L_anchor = lambda * (1 - cos(mu_normal_batch, c0)) with pre-registered lambda=0.5 (same order as the existing 0.25 group weight), optionally plus per-sequence cosine on pooled normal embeddings. One full 600-epoch curriculum retrain, otherwise identical to baseline.
decisive_experiments.pre_registered_success: Stage-4 normal-anchor cosine >= 0.85 (drift <= 0.10, roughly halving the baseline 0.406 drop); Stage-4 std >= 0.35 (no collapse); video-disjoint 5-class macro-F1 within 0.05 of baseline (0.495); each new-condition probe not degraded >5% relative.

decisive_experiments.name: Anchor-directional EWC (parameter-space consolidation)
decisive_experiments.what: At Stage 0, compute a diagonal Fisher information F over the view-encoder parameters from the normal-only corpus (squared gradients of JEPA+VICReg). During Stages 1-4 add L_ewc = (lambda/2) * sum_i F_i (theta_i - theta_i_0)^2, with pre-registered lambda. Anchor-directional variant: restrict the penalty to the top-k directions that most move the normal centroid, tying the penalty to the anchor metric rather than all parameters.
decisive_experiments.cost: ~20 min (Fisher is one extra forward/backward pass)
decisive_experiments.pre_registered_success: Same thresholds as R1 (anchor >= 0.85, std >= 0.35, probe non-inferiority); also report the anchor-directional vs vanilla-diagonal difference as a secondary result.
decisive_experiments.key_metric: Stage-4 normal-anchor cosine and drift slope vs baseline

decisive_experiments.name: Group-margin ablation (localize the drift source)
decisive_experiments.what: Identical curriculum with the label-aware group term disabled (group weight 0.25 -> 0, so Stages 1-4 run pure JEPA+VICReg). Tests whether the separation margin — which pushes condition centroids toward cosine 0.5 — is the active cause of drift rather than the new-task data stream itself.
decisive_experiments.pre_registered_success: If Stage-4 anchor cosine stays >= 0.85 with no consolidation term, drift is causally attributed to the label-aware margin objective (the headline mechanistic claim); if it still drops, forgetting is driven by the SSL stream itself, which is itself informative.

effort_and_feasibility: One baseline (already frozen, seconds to re-verify) plus 3 curriculum retrains x ~20 min ≈ 1 hour of wall-clock compute on this machine. Each intervention is a small edit to notebook 04's training loop: AnchorDist is ~30 lines (freeze Stage-0 target encoder, cache c0, add one cosine term with pre-registered lambda=0.5); anchor-directional EWC is ~40 lines (one diagonal-Fisher pass over normal data at Stage 0, then a weighted quadratic penalty); the margin-off ablation is a one-line config flag (group weight 0.25 -> 0). Frozen-embedding probes are seconds and the source_disjoint_probe GroupKFold ridge helper already exists. Realistic schedule: ~0.5 day to implement and pre-register thresholds in a written plan, ~0.5 day to run all retrains (overnight or in parallel), ~1 day to produce the drift-curve figure, metric table, and 5-page writeup, leaving ~1 day of buffer before Sep 5 AoE. The must-run minimum is R1 + R3 (2 retrains); drop R2 if any step slips.
main_risks: Interventions may not move the drift (informative null): distillation/EWC at lambda=0.5 could be too weak against the margin term. Mitigated by the margin-off ablation (R3), which still yields a publishable mechanistic finding even if R1/R2 fail.

Over-freezing: consolidation could raise the anchor cosine only by collapsing the normal representation or suppressing new-condition separation, tripping the non-inferiority plasticity threshold. Pre-registered retained/new-task probes catch this and turn it into a measured consolidation-plasticity tradeoff.

Anchor overfit/trivial memorization: because the anchor is computed on training rows, distillation can satisfy the geometric metric without meaningful retention. Guarded by reporting functional retention (source-disjoint probes) alongside the geometric anchor.

Provenance confound entrenches: the normal anchor mixes 12 canonical (one video) and 63 added-normal (different extraction path) sequences, so consolidating it may freeze the added-extraction style rather than true normal gait. Decompose the anchor into canonical vs added sub-anchors and report both.

Transductive exposure and small n: probes remain descriptive (encoder saw all rows) and some conditions have 1-2 videos, so no unbiased generalization claim is possible; the paper must carry the audit's honesty caveats and name held-out-video encoder retraining as future work.
Single pre-registered lambda per intervention risks a null-for-the-wrong-reason; no lambda sweep fits the run budget, so the paper reports one threshold-checked lambda rather than a tuned optimum.
paper_outline_5p: §1 Introduction (0.7p) — Clinical motivation: a deployed gait model keeps absorbing new conditions and must not forget the 'normal' reference (a safety property). Define the normal-anchor drift metric and state the measured baseline (0.954 -> 0.594). Hypothesis: drift = consolidation failure; cheap consolidation signals can repair it. Contributions bulleted. §2 Related work (0.5p) — S-JEPA/I-JEPA/V-JEPA, VICReg, continual-learning consolidation families (EWC, LwF/distillation, replay, functional regularization); note the near-absence of drift-quantified consolidation in skeleton/biosignal SSL — the gap. §3 Method (1p) — Compressed curriculum (159 seq, 5 stages, 11,400 updates, JEPA + 0.05·VICReg + 0.25·group); the normal-anchor definition and drift-rate slope; the three interventions (AnchorDist, anchor-directional EWC, replay/upweight) with pre-registered lambda and success thresholds; the margin-off ablation. §4 Results (1.5p) — Baseline drift curve; overlaid intervention drift curves; metric table (anchor cosine, drift slope, std, pair-cosine, retained 5-class and new-condition source-disjoint probe acc); margin-off ablation attributing drift to the label-aware separation margin; representative geometry figure. §5 Discussion & limitations (0.8p) — What cheap consolidation can and cannot do at this scale; the consolidation-plasticity tradeoff; generalization caveat (transductive, provenance confound, 1-2 videos per class) and the held-out-video retrain as future work; conclusion that 'don't forget normal' is a measurable, repairable, and pre-registerable property. References excluded per format.
recommendation: Proceed — this is the strongest 5-page bet available in the 3-day window. It converts the project's one clean, quantified, pre-registered negative result into the paper's core finding, requires zero new data and ~1 hour of compute, maps one-to-one onto the CFP's 'continual learning in biosignals' topic, and has a built-in publishable fallback (the margin-off ablation) if the interventions underperform. Minimum viable execution = baseline re-verification + AnchorDist + margin-off ablation (2 retrains); add anchor-directional EWC as the third run if the schedule holds. Pre-register thresholds in a written plan before launching any retrain, and keep every probe caveat (transductive, provenance, small-n) explicit in the paper.
